subject: Civil Engineering
title: What Is Concrete?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is Concrete?.

hook.text: Concrete is the most used material on Earth after water. We pour 30 billion tons a year.

buildup.text: It's a mixture of cement, water, sand, and gravel — simple ingredients, remarkable strength.

discovery.text: Cement is the glue. When mixed with water, it hardens through a chemical reaction.

twist.text: Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension — it cracks when pulled apart.

climax.text: That weakness led to reinforced concrete — steel handles tension, concrete handles compression.

punchline.text: Mix rocks, sand, cement, and water — and build civilization.

quiz.question: What is concrete's fundamental weakness?
options: It dissolves in water over time
It is strong in compression but weak in tension — it cracks under pulling forces
It cannot withstand temperatures above 100 degrees Fahrenheit
